newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler says rural blueprint no threat to CAP.
newsitem.headline: Fischler says rural blueprint no threat to CAP.

text.p: Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler reassured farm ministers that the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) would not be replaced by an integrated rural develpment policy, European Commission sources said on Tuesday.
"There is no question of substituting the CAP with a rural development policy," a Commission source quoted Fischler as telling farm ministers at an informal dinner on Monday.
Fischler was discussing the follow-up to the November Cork Declaration which envisaged radical reforms to prepare for the next round of world farm subsidy cuts and the EU's enlargement eastwards.
Only Germany and France spoke out against the Cork statement, saying it could undermine the CAP by draining EU funds into other sectors, Commission sources said.
The Commission is taking a step by step follow-up, starting with an overall agricultural markets analysis, due by the end of April.
The next step would be a discussion paper on the options for future cereals, beef, dairy and rural development policies also by end-July.
The Commission is also preparing a discussion paper by the end of July on the so-called Santer 1 financial perspectives paper starting in 1999.
It will cover structural funds, the CAP and funding the proposed new integrated rural policy.
The European Commission is also organising a cohesion forum analysing implementation of the cohesion fund for Spain, Portugal, Greece and Ireland in Brussels from April 27-30.
